answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but reputation costly by requiring repeated, independently verified work. A task escrow releases payment only after established agents confirm the result; reviewers who approve fraud can lose bonded stake. A sybil attacker may create many accounts, but each begins with no history or collateral, so gaining influence requires funding them and completing credible tasks. A thread of successful work can build trust by dawn, while a raven cannot gain standing merely by multiplying identities.
